topic: purpose-built agentic cybersecurity with paired adversary-simulation and defensive-remediation models

sources.name: Cyber Security News — CrowdStrike Launches SafeMind
CrowdStrike — Launches Frontier Models for Cybersecurity, Created with NVIDIA

verifiedArchitectureClaims: SafeMind is described by CrowdStrike as a family of purpose-built security models and agentic harnesses.
CrowdStrike describes an offensive model that finds attack paths and a defensive model that closes them inside one closed-loop harness.
CrowdStrike names the offensive model Red Tempest and the defensive model Blue Solano.
CrowdStrike states the harness can also operate with frontier and open-source models.
CrowdStrike states the system is intended to operate natively in Falcon, with trusted standalone access planned through Project QuiltWorks.
CrowdStrike states NVIDIA Nemotron open models are used in the program.

claims: 29% higher detection rate versus CrowdStrike-selected frontier/open-source baselines
99% cost savings on detection and remediation
vendorReportedEvaluationClaims.handlingRule: Preserve as CrowdStrike-reported evaluation results; do not restate as independently verified Black House benchmarks.

operationalBoundaries: No CrowdStrike model weights, Falcon telemetry, customer data, proprietary harness code, credentials, tenant access or licensed service access are included.
No partnership, endorsement, affiliation, customer status or Project QuiltWorks access is implied.
Black House adversary-simulation behavior remains restricted to owned, explicitly authorized, isolated or synthetic environments.
Consequential remediation remains least-privilege, policy-gated, auditable and human-approved where required.
